title: Childhood homes and Jelly's house on Frenchman Street
summary: Photos of the Frenchman and Robertson house, the parade float, and later moves to Durban and St. Bernard.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: No, that's right. So he just slipped and— Well, I was going to ask about the different homes that you were raised. Now, according to Jell-Anne, he talks about a home— On Frenchman Street, doesn't he? A Frenchman and we're Robertson. And this is— Yeah, well, that's the— November is 1443 at the corner of Robertson. I just wondered if—
No, I wouldn't know anything about that. See, I wouldn't know. I was a baby.
And there's two other little pictures. There's a lot of dogs and everything on here, different ones. This is that same house taken from the side.

Yeah, but I mean, the house that— where he left from was on— Oh, isn't that pretty, though? It looks like it might have been on Frenchman Street. Well, this was on Frenchman and Robertson. It's still there. That's still there. Because that's what they had on the float this year, on that parade float. Oh, is that right? They had his home, and then they had the part of the— I didn't see that. I wish I'd seen that. And I forget whose parade it was. It was on the first parade that was— No, it's too bad I missed it. And what is this?
Oh, that's over in Algiers. Oh, I see. That's the Musicians' Union Building. Oh, yeah. But those are the two houses that were supposed to be the one where he lived, Mm-hmm.
Well, this one is. I know this one from a fact. That's the same place.
Yeah, it's just smaller. That's the side of it. But you don't remember that house? No, I don't remember that. Then you went and lived other places—

No, my grandmother moved on Durban Street. On Durban Street, and later on, we moved two or three doors from an uncle of mine in the 1300 block of St. Bernard Avenue. St. Bernard. Yes. She wanted to be close to her children all the time. You see, after my aunt started having children, she thought they would go to themselves, and my aunt never did leave her. Yes. Mm-hmm. Do you have a picture of my house that they took— No. —during the—you know when they made this Shades of New Orleans? No, I didn't get to see that. Oh, I see. They took the picture of this house, too. No, I didn't. And most of the inside, because I had a dining room here, and they brought the mirrors close to the front, but they couldn't put the lights on it.
